title: shared_ptr and weak_ptr
lesson:
Sometimes one owner isn't the truth. A texture is used by twenty sprites; it should stay loaded while **any** of them needs it and be freed when the **last** one is gone. That is **shared ownership**, and `std::shared_ptr` does it.

```
auto tex = std::make_shared<Texture>("grass.png");
auto a = tex;              // copying is allowed: now 2 owners
auto b = tex;              // 3 owners
tex.use_count();           // 3
a.reset();                 // a lets go: 2
// when the last shared_ptr goes, the Texture is deleted
```

Inside, the shared_ptr keeps a **reference count**. Every copy adds one, every destroyed or reset copy takes one away, and at zero the object is deleted. It is RAII again, with a counter.

**Prefer unique_ptr.** Shared ownership is harder to reason about ("who is keeping this alive?") and the counting costs a little. Use `shared_ptr` only when there really are several owners with no clear "last one".

**Watching without owning: weak_ptr.** An enemy follows the player. Should the enemy **own** the player? No: if the player leaves the game, the player should go, and the enemy should notice. A `std::weak_ptr` points at something owned by shared_ptrs **without** adding to the count:

```
std::weak_ptr<Player> target = player;   // doesn't keep the player alive
if (auto p = target.lock()) {            // lock(): a shared_ptr, or empty if gone
    moveToward(p->x);
} else {
    wander();                            // the player was destroyed
}
target.expired();                        // true once the player is gone
```

Always `lock()` and check: the thing may have been destroyed since you last looked.

**Cycles: the shared_ptr trap.** A squad owns its soldiers (`shared_ptr<Soldier>`), and each soldier points back at its squad. If that back pointer is also a `shared_ptr`, the squad keeps the soldiers alive and the soldiers keep the squad alive. When the rest of the game lets go, the counts never reach zero and **nothing is ever deleted**: a leak that no `delete` can fix, because there are none to fix.

The rule: **owners point down with shared_ptr (or unique_ptr); back-pointers and "I'm watching you" pointers use weak_ptr.** Parent owns child; child watches parent.

In Unreal, `TSharedPtr` and `TWeakPtr` work the same way, and for actors there is `TWeakObjectPtr<AActor>`, which is exactly the "enemy follows a target that may be destroyed" pointer.

notes: make_shared creates the Player with one owner; copying the shared_ptr makes another.
use_count is the number of owners. The weak_ptr doesn't change it.
The Player is deleted when the last shared_ptr resets, not the first.
lock() gives a usable shared_ptr only if the Player still exists, so the enemy can react safely.

exercises.title: A texture cache
exercises.prompt:
Write class TextureCache, which keeps a std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<Texture>>:
- std::shared_ptr<Texture> load(const std::string& file): if that file is already in the cache, return the same shared_ptr; otherwise create it with std::make_shared, store it and return it.
- int loadedCount() const: how many textures the cache holds.
- void unloadUnused(): removes every texture that only the cache is holding (its use_count() is 1).

tests.call: []{ TextureCache c; auto a = c.load("grass.png"); auto b = c.load("grass.png"); return a == b; }()
tests.hint_if_fail: The second load of the same file must return the stored pointer, not a new Texture.

tests.call: []{ TextureCache c; auto a = c.load("grass.png"); auto b = c.load("grass.png"); return a.use_count(); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: The cache, a and b all own the same Texture.

tests.call: []{ TextureCache c; c.load("a.png"); c.load("b.png"); c.load("a.png"); return c.loadedCount(); }()
[]{ int before = Texture::alive; TextureCache c; auto keep = c.load("a.png"); c.load("b.png"); c.unloadUnused(); return c.loadedCount() * 10 + (Texture::alive - before); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: b.png is held only by the cache, so unloadUnused removes it; a.png is still used by keep.

tests.call: []{ int before = Texture::alive; { TextureCache c; c.load("x.png"); c.load("y.png"); } return Texture::alive - before; }()

hints: load: auto it = textures.find(file); if (it != textures.end()) return it->second;
Otherwise: auto t = std::make_shared<Texture>(file); textures[file] = t; return t;
unloadUnused: walk with an iterator; if (it->second.use_count() == 1) it = textures.erase(it); else ++it;

exercises.title: An enemy that follows a player
exercises.prompt:
Follower currently OWNS its target, so a player who leaves the game is kept alive by the enemies chasing them. Change it to watch the player with a std::weak_ptr<Player>:
- void follow(const std::shared_ptr<Player>& p) starts watching p.
- bool hasTarget() const: true only while the player still exists.
- std::string targetName() const: the player's name, or "none".
- int stepToward(int myX) const: moves one step toward the player's x (myX + 1 or myX - 1, or myX if already there). With no target it returns myX.

tests.call: []{ auto p = std::make_shared<Player>("Amina", 5); Follower f; f.follow(p); return p.use_count(); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: A follower must not own the player: use std::weak_ptr<Player>.

tests.call: []{ auto p = std::make_shared<Player>("Amina", 5); Follower f; f.follow(p); return f.targetName(); }()
[]{ auto p = std::make_shared<Player>("Amina", 5); Follower f; f.follow(p); p.reset(); return f.hasTarget(); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: Once the last owner lets go, the player is gone; check with lock() or expired().

tests.call: []{ auto p = std::make_shared<Player>("Juma", 5); Follower f; f.follow(p); return std::to_string(f.stepToward(2)) + "," + std::to_string(f.stepToward(9)) + "," + std::to_string(f.stepToward(5)); }()
[]{ auto p = std::make_shared<Player>("Juma", 5); Follower f; f.follow(p); p.reset(); return f.targetName() + "," + std::to_string(f.stepToward(2)); }()

tests.why: Store the target as a std::weak_ptr<Player>.

hints: Change the member to std::weak_ptr<Player> target;
Elsewhere: if (auto p = target.lock()) { ... use p->x ... } else { no target }

exercises.title: Break the squad cycle
exercises.prompt: A Squad owns its Soldiers, and each Soldier points back at its Squad with a shared_ptr. That is a cycle: when the game lets go of a squad, neither the squad nor its soldiers are ever deleted. Fix it by making Soldier::squad a std::weak_ptr<Squad>, and update squadOf so it returns the squad's name, or "none" if the squad no longer exists. enlist(squad, name) and squadOf(soldier) keep the same signatures.

tests.call: []{ auto sq = std::make_shared<Squad>("Red"); auto s = enlist(sq, "Juma"); return squadOf(*s); }()
[]{ int b1 = Squad::alive, b2 = Soldier::alive; { auto sq = std::make_shared<Squad>("Red"); enlist(sq, "Juma"); enlist(sq, "Otieno"); } return (Squad::alive - b1) * 10 + (Soldier::alive - b2); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: Squad and soldiers keep each other alive. The back-pointer must not own: weak_ptr.

tests.call: []{ auto sq = std::make_shared<Squad>("Red"); enlist(sq, "Juma"); enlist(sq, "Amina"); return sq.use_count(); }()
[]{ std::shared_ptr<Soldier> s; { auto sq = std::make_shared<Squad>("Blue"); s = enlist(sq, "Wanjiru"); } return squadOf(*s); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: The squad is gone, so lock() gives an empty pointer: return "none".

tests.why: Make the soldier's back-pointer a std::weak_ptr<Squad>.

hints: Only one line in Soldier changes: std::weak_ptr<Squad> squad;
squadOf can't use s.squad->name any more: if (auto sq = s.squad.lock()) return sq->name; return "none";

quiz.q: Three shared_ptrs own a Texture. Two are reset. Is the Texture deleted?
quiz.why: It is deleted when the count reaches zero.

quiz.q: Does copying a weak_ptr from a shared_ptr change use_count?
How do you safely use what a weak_ptr points at?
choices: auto p = w.lock(); then check p
quiz.why: lock() gives a shared_ptr, empty if the object is gone.

quiz.q: A parent and child hold shared_ptrs to each other. What happens when the rest of the program lets go?
quiz.why: Each keeps the other's count above zero: a cycle.

quiz.q: Which should you reach for first for a game entity with one clear owner?
quiz.why: One owner: unique_ptr. Use shared_ptr only for real shared ownership.

cards.a: Owners point down with shared_ptr; back-pointers use weak_ptr.

explain: Explain why an enemy should watch its target with a weak_ptr rather than own it with a shared_ptr.
